title: Punctuation-as-Pitch: Rising Surprise Contour
speaker: astra
wording_and_punctuation_change: Wording changed from rigid formal declarative ('That is unexpected.') to conversational preface ('Wait, ... Let me check right away.'). Punctuation replaced standard period with the interrobang ('?!') followed by a comma. In Rime Coda, '? !' triggers a rapid +65 Hz fundamental frequency (F0) rising contour that signals human surprise, whereas a terminal period produces a descending, flat pitch decay.

variant_a.label: Flat / Monotone Syntax
variant_a.text: Did flight UA 402 divert. That is unexpected.

variant_b.label: Rime-Optimized Ear Syntax
variant_b.text: Wait, did flight UA 402 divert?! Let me check right away.

title: Acoustic Cadence: Natural Hesitation vs Robotic Delivery
speaker: astra
wording_and_punctuation_change: Added informal discourse marker ('Let's see...') and active continuous phrasing ('locking in'). Punctuation added ellipsis ('...') and standardized lowercase dotted time notation ('7:00 p.m.'). In Rime Coda, three dots ('...') introduce a 180ms hesitation pause with natural breath inflection, preventing the rushed cadence of Variant A while keeping LiveKit endpointing silence timers stable.

variant_a.label: Flat / Stiff Delivery
variant_a.text: Checking reservation BK 5521 for party of four at 7 PM.

variant_b.label: Rime-Optimized Ear Syntax
variant_b.text: Let's see... locking in reservation BK 5521 for four at 7:00 p.m.

title: Self-Correction Cadence: Trail-Off Hyphen vs Formal Indecision
speaker: astra
wording_and_punctuation_change: Wording changed from passive disjunction ('or maybe') to an active command with corrective modifier ('Head toward ... actually, make that ...'). Punctuation introduced a double trail-off hyphen ('--'). In Rime Coda, the double hyphen creates a glottal cut-off with a slight pitch drop, realistically mimicking a human dispatcher interrupting their own thought mid-sentence to correct a gate assignment.

variant_a.label: Formal Indecisive Sentence
variant_a.text: Proceed to Gate B12 or maybe Gate B14.

variant_b.label: Rime-Optimized Ear Syntax
variant_b.text: Head toward Gate B12-- actually, make that Gate B14.

title: Financial Syntax: Phonetic Expansion vs Raw Text
speaker: astra
wording_and_punctuation_change: Wording and punctuation change: Symbolic currency prefix ('$150.00') normalized to spoken wording ('150 dollars'), eliminating decimal punctuation and awkward zero cents recitation ('one hundred fifty dollars and zero cents'). Result is a 32% faster, crisper vocal delivery that sounds completely natural over a noisy radio link.

variant_a.label: Raw Written Syntax
variant_a.text: The total fee is $150.00 for the permit.

variant_b.label: Rime-Optimized Ear Syntax
variant_b.text: The total fee is 150 dollars for the permit.
